units.passage: For every assignment or project where GENAI is utilized, students must submit a brief reflective statement (approximately 150-200 words) describing:
units.why: A required 'brief reflective statement (approximately 150-200 words)' per assignment is a reflection submission (P26).

units.passage: Report on AI’s role. Submit prompts and brief statements on how using AI enhanced your analysis indicating how AI tools informed your process and the final product, including what prompts you used and how you validated any AI-generated citations
units.why: 'Submit prompts and brief statements on how using AI enhanced your analysis' requires prompts plus a reflection statement (P26).

units.passage: I used [name of AI tool] to help me [explain how you used it].
units.why: The sample 'Use acknowledgment' template asks students to write 'I used [name of AI tool] to help me [explain how you used it]. It did [...] well. I had to change [...]', with a note on whether they would use it again. This is a template for a reflection on AI use attached to the work, addressed to students during work: P26 (reflection/log).

units.passage: Include a copy of the prompts and output with your final submission (you can do this by printing the webpage as a PDF).
units.why: 'Include a copy of the prompts and output with your final submission' is a transcript requirement (P26).

units.passage: The project will have a reflection with screenshots asking students to record the steps they took in relation to AI use.
units.why: 'The project will have a reflection with screenshots' requires reflection and screenshots of AI use (P26).

units.passage: The project and the use of AI will be further discussed in the final reflection submitted at the end of the semester as well.
units.why: 'further discussed in the final reflection' is a second reflection at semester end (P26).

units.passage: Provide a Rationale and Reflection: At the end of the assignment, submit the following: 1) a brief rationale (100-150 words) explaining how you used the GenAI tool to assist you with the assignment and explain why its use was appropriate, and 2) a brief reflection (100-150 words) explaining how using the GenAI tools affected your learning and/or process involved in completing the assignment. A caution about AI: It is important to remember that AI-generated content is not always reliable and accurate.
units.why: 'submit ... a brief rationale (100-150 words) ... and a brief reflection (100-150 words)' (P26).

units.passage: Provide a Rationale and Reflection: At the end of the assignment, submit the following: 1) a brief rationale (100-150 words) explaining how you used the GenAI tool to assist you with the assignment and explain why its use was appropriate, and 2) a brief reflection (100-150 words) explaining how using the GenAI tools affected your learning and/or process involved in completing the assignment. A caution about AI: It is important to remember that AI-generated content is not always reliable and accurate.
units.why: Students submit 'a brief reflection' on how AI affected learning: P26.

units.passage: Students may be asked to save the AI chat as a PDF file for verification.
units.why: College of Business: 'may be asked to save the AI chat as a PDF file': P26.

units.passage: You’ll be asked to reflect frequently about AI usage both in-class and as part of your assignment submission (see assignment instructions for specifics), where you’ll also be asked to share your prompts, screenshots of your chats with Generative AI tools, and how you ensure your ideas and voice remain central in your assignment.
units.why: Students must 'share your prompts, screenshots of your chats' and reflect on use; logs and reflections submitted (P26).

units.passage: When using Generative AI in this way, you’ll be expected to maintain the various iterations of your written work so that you can reflect on the changes you incorporate based on suggestions from the Generative AI model and demonstrate how you negotiated between Generative AI writing and your own.
units.why: Students must keep drafts to reflect on changes from AI; keeping drafts and reflections (P26).

units.passage: This statement should be created without the use of Generative AI and should be your own reflection.
units.why: The disclosure statement must be written without AI; this is a rule on the reflection itself, nearest P26 (reflections).
units.fit_note: Says the reflection must be AI-free rather than that one is required.

units.passage: You’ll be asked to reflect frequently about AI usage both in-class and as part of your assignment submission (see assignment instructions for specifics), where you may also be asked to share your prompts, screenshots of your chats with Generative AI tools, and how you used Generative AI to prepare you to, by the end of the semester, independently (without the use of Generative AI) achieve the learning objectives of this course. If you have any questions about this policy, please talk with me. Consequences for Violating the Generative AI Usage Policy: Deviating from the acknowledgement, citation, and reflection guidelines described here may be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy of this course.
units.why: Students "may also be asked to share your prompts, screenshots of your chats," a possible transcript requirement (P26).
units.fit_note: Reflection is expected; sharing prompts and screenshots may be asked.

units.passage: You’ll be asked to reflect frequently about your Generative AI usage, including your process, how you assess accuracy, and how you combine human innovation with Generative AI. Review assignment guidelines carefully for what you should be documenting as you use Generative AI, as well as how Generative AI may or may not be used in your reflection process. If you ever have any questions about this policy, please talk with me. Consequences for Violating the Generative AI Usage Policy: Deviating from the documentation and reflection guidelines provided in each assignment may be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy of this course.
units.why: Students reflect on process, accuracy assessment and combining human innovation with AI; reflections (P26).

units.passage: Have students reflect on their assignment process. Metacognitive activities reveal authentic student work.
units.why: 'Have students reflect on their assignment process' asks instructors to collect reflections on the process, which is the reflection part of P26; it is an assignment-design device, noted in the fit note.
units.fit_note: Also an assignment-design suggestion to discourage reliance on AI ('Metacognitive activities reveal authentic student work'); the other coder judged it P35. / Reflection used to reveal authentic work rather than to report AI use.

units.passage: Keep drafts of your work to show how AI was used to complete the assignment.
units.why: 'Keep drafts of your work to show how AI was used to complete the assignment' (P26).

units.passage: Add specific requirements for AI use. For example: you are required to keep drafts of assignments and generative AI logs that demonstrate how you used AI and what portion of an assignment's content was generated by AI.
units.why: The example 'you are required to keep drafts of assignments and generative AI logs' shows a required record of AI use: P26.
units.fit_note: Given as example template wording that instructors may adopt.

units.passage: Students could embed screenshots of AI output, submit transcripts of AI interactions, or share the prompts they entered.
units.why: "Students could embed screenshots of AI output, submit transcripts of AI interactions, or share the prompts they entered" lists transcripts and prompts as documentation (P26).
units.fit_note: Offers options an instructor may require, among them screenshots and prompts.

units.passage: Less formally, you may ask students to submit an AI-assisted learning disclosure or reflection
units.why: "you may ask students to submit an AI-assisted learning disclosure or reflection" is a lighter disclosure option, so P26.

units.passage: Along with your completed assignment, you are required to submit an AI-Assisted Learning Disclosure acknowledging the ways you did or did not use generative AI assistance. There are no “correct” answers.
units.why: "acknowledging the ways you did or did not use generative AI assistance" is a required AI-Assisted Learning Disclosure reflection submitted with the assignment (P26).

units.passage: as well as separately document and attach your prompts, dialogue, and iterations with the AI for each assignment.
units.why: "separately document and attach your prompts, dialogue, and iterations with the AI for each assignment" requires submitting a log of the interaction, so P26.

units.passage: I have reviewed and edited this work and have retained records of my generative AI use.
units.why: The template says 'I have reviewed and edited this work and have retained records of my generative AI use.' Students attest that they kept records. Records are kept, not submitted, so P26 is only a partial fit.
units.fit_note: Students attest that they kept records; the template does not require submitting them, and also has them attest to reviewing and editing the work. / Students attest to retaining records and to having reviewed and edited the work; records are not required to be submitted.

units.passage: Justificación detallada del uso de IA en el proceso. Reflexión crítica sobre la calidad y relevancia de los resultados generados.
units.policy: Level 3 requires a detailed justification of AI use in the process and a critical reflection on the quality and relevance of the generated results.
units.why: Level 3 requires a detailed justification of AI use and a critical reflection on results; a reflection submitted with the work, so P26.
units.fit_note: Also requires a detailed justification of AI use in the process. | Also requires a justification of the use, not only a reflection.

units.passage: Es fundamental documentar cómo se utilizó la IA para diseñar estrategias novedosas y qué impacto tuvo en los resultados finales.
units.why: Sample text says it is "fundamental documentar cómo se utilizó la IA" and what impact it had; documentation duty, so P26.
units.fit_note: Documentation of how AI was used and its impact, not necessarily full transcripts.

units.passage: In courses where GenAI is allowed, instructors may require transparency, such as students acknowledging their use or providing transcripts of their AI interactions.
units.why: Instructors "may require ... acknowledging their use or providing transcripts of their AI interactions". Transcripts are the most specific element: P26; acknowledgment is P24.
units.fit_note: Coder A (P26): Also covers acknowledgment of use (P24); instructor-optional. / Coder B (P26): Also covers acknowledging use (P24); optional for instructors rather than mandatory.

units.passage: Likewise, if you use a chat model, you are required to include a link to your chat history (if available) or paste in a transcript of the conversation (if not).
units.why: "you are required to include a link to your chat history ... or paste in a transcript of the conversation" requires submitting transcripts: P26.

units.passage: Please be sure to include your own actual observations and reflections in your self-reflection submissions, though you are also encouraged to use Gen AI to enhance those as well.
units.why: "include your own actual observations and reflections in your self-reflection submissions" requires reflections that are the student's own while AI may enhance them; P26 (reflections) is nearest but this is about authentic content.
units.fit_note: Self-reflections are required and must contain the student's own observations; AI may be used to enhance them. / Requires the student's own reflections, not reflections on AI use.

units.passage: A resource faculty can use to help students document how they used AI in their coursework.
units.why: SAID is 'A resource faculty can use to help students document how they used AI in their coursework', supporting student documentation of AI use (P26).
units.fit_note: A resource for documenting use, not a requirement to keep transcripts or reflections. A disclosure resource offered to instructors; the passage does not require students to submit transcripts.

units.passage: Documenting your verification process for AI-generated citations (for example, creating an audit trail by tracking the AI tools used, prompts, exact steps taken to independently verify every claim and citation generated by AI against authentic, original materials).
units.why: 'Documenting your verification process ... creating an audit trail by tracking the AI tools used, prompts'; keeping records of AI use, P26.
units.fit_note: The audit trail is for verification of AI-generated citations in research.

units.passage: To ensure that you can demonstrate ownership of the assignments you submit, you are encouraged to maintain clear evidence of your work (e.g., time-stamped drafts and notes; copies and links to source material).
units.why: Students 'are encouraged to maintain clear evidence of your work (e.g., time-stamped drafts and notes)'; keeping drafts (P26), but as proof of ownership, not AI use.
units.fit_note: Evidence is kept to show ownership of work in a no-AI course, not to log AI use; drafts are kept as evidence and not necessarily submitted.

units.passage: When usingArtificial Intelligencetools on assignments, add an appendix showing (a) the entire exchange, highlighting the most relevant sections; (b) a description of precisely whichArtificial Intelligencetools were used (e.g. ChatGPT private subscription version or DALL-E free version), (c) an explanation of how theArtificial Intelligencetools were used (e.g. to generate ideas, turns of phrase, elements of text, long stretches of text, lines of argument, pieces of evidence, maps of the conceptual territory, illustrations of key concepts, etc.); (d) an account of whyArtificial Intelligencetools were used (e.g. to save time, to surmount writer’s block, to stimulate thinking, to handle mounting stress, to clarify prose, to translate text, to experiment for fun,
units.why: Sample appendix: 'add an appendix showing (a) the entire exchange ... (b) a description of precisely which tools were used ... (c) how ... (d) why'; transcript plus tool and purpose, P26.
units.fit_note: Also asks for the tool used, how and why it was used (P25, P24).

units.passage: and the relationship between those sections and student contributions should be discussed in cover letters that accompany the essay submission.
units.why: Sample: the relationship between AI-generated sections and student contributions 'should be discussed in cover letters'; a reflection on AI use submitted with the work, P26.

units.passage: Have students submit their prompt and the improved chatGPT response with their added content highlighted.
units.why: Example assignment 2e tells the instructor to "Have students submit their prompt and the improved chatGPT response with their added content highlighted." It is addressed to instructors designing an assignment (an example, not a USC requirement), and the design requires students to hand in their prompt and output, which is P26.

units.passage: Requesting drafts, annotations, or reflections on decision-making.
units.policy: When GenAI use is suspected, instructors may request drafts, annotations or reflections on decision-making.
units.why: "Requesting drafts, annotations, or reflections on decision-making" asks students for process evidence and reflections, so P26.
units.fit_note: Asks students for drafts and reflections after suspicion (cf. P26). | Used by the instructor as a response to suspicion, not as a standing student duty.

units.passage: Documenting the process with rough drafts and revisions to track the progress of a student's work
units.policy: Instructors can have students document the process with rough drafts and revisions to track the progress of their work, as a way to ensure students create their own work.
units.why: "Documenting the process with rough drafts and revisions" asks students to keep drafts as process evidence, closest to P26 (drafts), though the page frames it as an assignment design idea.
units.fit_note: Framed as an instructor assignment-design idea for tracking progress, not a rule that students submit AI-use logs. / Process documentation proposed as assignment design, not a disclosure of AI use.

units.passage: In courses where your instructor allows use, keep a log of your GenAI use; the university has recommended that instructors who allow GenAI use ask students to document it.
units.why: Where use is allowed, students should 'keep a log of your GenAI use', noting the university recommends instructors ask students to document use: logs, P26.

units.passage: Reflect on your use of GenAI: How are you using it? What does it offer you as a writer? What are you learning about writing while using GenAI? Is using GenAI helping you make better choices as a writer–and if so, how? What are your concerns about using GenAI during the writing process? What is your ethical stance on using GenAI in certain writing situations; for example, given its impact on the environment, when do you consider GenAI use warranted?
units.why: Students should 'reflect on your use of GenAI', asking how it helps and what ethical stance they hold: reflections, P26. [Reconciled: phase=during-work.]
units.fit_note: Reflection prompts also cover ethics and environmental impact; nothing says the reflection must be submitted. | Other coder: Reflection is for the student's own learning; no submission required.

units.passage: the relationship between those sections and student contributions should be discussed in cover letters
units.why: Sample (Iowa): AI-generated essay parts appear in a different colour and the relationship to student work "should be discussed in cover letters"; reflection submitted with work, P26.

units.passage: AI may be used freely with transparent acknowledgement, documentation of prompts and prompt evolution, and a reflective evaluation of the output and your revisions to it.
units.policy: AI may be used freely with transparent acknowledgement, documentation of prompts and prompt evolution, and a reflective evaluation of the output and the student's revisions to it.
units.why: 'Yes, and here's how': 'AI may be used freely with transparent acknowledgement, documentation of prompts and prompt evolution, and a reflective evaluation'. An open level whose condition is documented prompts and reflection, so P26; the level scheme is coded once as P05 at the framework unit.
units.fit_note: Combines free use with acknowledgement and reflection.

units.passage: Prompt self-reflection, encouraging students to critically evaluate their use of AI and its impact on their learning outcomes
units.why: 'encouraging students to critically evaluate their use of AI and its impact' recommends that instructors prompt student reflection on their own AI use, which is the kind of reflection P26 covers; the unit is a should for instructors addressed to student reflection, with no submission required.
units.fit_note: An instructor prompt for self-reflection, not a requirement to submit a reflection. / Suggests instructors prompt reflection on AI use; no required submission is stated.

units.passage: Assignments can encourage transparency by asking students to document how they used AI tools, what specific prompts or inputs they provided, and how the outputs were refined or integrated into their work
units.why: 'asking students to document how they used AI tools, what specific prompts or inputs they provided' recommends process documentation, so P26.

units.passage: asking students to submit a transcript of their AI tutoring session as a formative assessment
units.why: 'You might consider asking students to submit a transcript of their AI tutoring session as a formative assessment' asks for transcripts, P26.

units.passage: Accountability also involves documenting decisions made with AI tools to maintain traceability.
units.why: 'Accountability also involves documenting decisions made with AI tools to maintain traceability' is a record-keeping duty; closest to P26 (keep logs) but it concerns decisions, not student transcripts.
units.fit_note: Documents decisions made with AI for traceability, not chat logs or reflections submitted with work.

units.passage: The submitted work should include the exact prompt you used to generate the content and the AI’s complete response as an appendix.
units.why: Students 'should include the exact prompt' and 'complete response as an appendix', which is a transcript submission: P26 (P25 would cover only the citation detail).
units.fit_note: Delivered as an appendix of the full exchange, close to P26.

units.passage: and the relationship between those sections and student contributions should be discussed in a cover letter that accompanies the assignment when submitted.
units.why: "the relationship between those sections and student contributions should be discussed in a cover letter" requires a reflection on AI use, P26.

units.passage: When using AI tools for assignments, add an appendix showing (a) the entire exchange (e.g., prompts used), highlighting the most relevant sections;
units.why: Students must 'add an appendix showing... the entire exchange (e.g., prompts used)': a transcript requirement (P26).

units.passage: (c) an explanation of how the AI tools were used (e.g. to generate ideas, elements of text, etc.);
units.why: The appendix must explain 'how the AI tools were used', a reflection on use (P26).

units.passage: (d) an account of why AI tools were used (e.g. to save time, to surmount writer’s block, to stimulate thinking, to experiment for fun, etc.).
units.why: The appendix must give 'an account of why AI tools were used', a reflection on motives (P26).

units.passage: What you did with the output (e.g., "Considered its suggestions but developed my own outline," "Used one suggestion to revise my introduction")
units.why: The acknowledgment must say "What you did with the output"; a short reflection on use, P26 as closest.
units.fit_note: A short statement of what was done with the output, not full transcripts.

units.passage: You should also reflect on the impact of any AI use on your learning process.
units.why: Students "should also reflect on the impact of any AI use on your learning process"; a reflection duty, P26 with partial fit since it is not submitted.
units.fit_note: Reflection is asked but not stated to be submitted. A self-reflection duty about learning impact, not a submitted reflection. Asks students to reflect; does not say the reflection is submitted.

units.passage: How you evaluated/modified the output: (e.g., "Fact-checked all statistics against original sources," "Rewrote the logic to better fit my argument")
units.why: The acknowledgment states "How you evaluated/modified the output", a short reflection, P26.
units.fit_note: A short note rather than full transcripts.

units.passage: What did you learn?
units.policy: The discussion of the AI contribution answers whether the output was revised, whether follow-up questions were asked, and what was learned.
units.why: 'What did you learn?' joins questions about revision and follow-ups that the discussion must answer: a reflection on AI use (P26).

units.passage: Write a brief paragraph at the end of your work explaining how and why you used ZotGPT.
units.why: 'Write a brief paragraph at the end of your work explaining how and why you used ZotGPT' is a required reflection on AI use (P26).

units.passage: My recommendation is to screen shot and save everything (i.e., what prompts you used, what answers were produced, where, why, and how).
units.why: 'My recommendation is to screen shot and save everything' advises keeping prompts and answers, a transcript practice (P26); recommended, not required.

units.passage: When using generative AI, keep a journal documenting prompts, AI responses, and your usage. Your instructor may ask you to provide this documentation.
units.policy: Students keep a journal documenting prompts, AI responses, and their usage, and the instructor may ask for this documentation.
units.why: "keep a journal documenting prompts, AI responses, and your usage" requires a log of AI use, P26, must.

units.passage: Depending on the course or requirements provided by the instructor/mentor/adviser, links to AI chat(s) may be submitted with the submission
units.why: 'links to AI chat(s) may be submitted with the submission' depending on the course means instructors may ask for chat logs: P26, with modality may because it is conditional.

units.passage: A design studio where teams use AI throughout the process (needs analysis prompts, content drafting, content generation, and draft refinement) to build a website for their project, combined with submitting an AI use log and critical reflection
units.why: The Level 4 design-studio example ends with 'submitting an AI use log and critical reflection', a log and reflection submitted with the work: P26.

units.passage: They produce a final report and document the process, including turning in their chat prompt logs
units.why: The same example ends with 'including turning in their chat prompt logs', so prompt logs are submitted with the report: P26.

units.passage: Ask students to reflect on how they used AI in an assignment
units.why: 'Ask students to reflect on how they used AI in an assignment' recommends reflections on AI use, and says to include them in the grade: P26.

units.passage: Students can be asked to reflect on how they used generative AI as part of completing the assignment
units.why: 'Students can be asked to reflect on how they used generative AI as part of completing the assignment' lets instructors require a write-up of AI use: P26.

units.passage: Note (if applicable) your AI documentation and citation requirements. This might include screenshots, transcripts, documents with track changes enabled,
units.why: 'Note (if applicable) your AI documentation and citation requirements. This might include screenshots, transcripts, documents with track changes enabled' lists documentation forms. P26 fits because transcripts and screenshots are named.
units.fit_note: Instructors are told to state documentation requirements; students are not directly told to keep transcripts.

units.passage: Students should save evidence of their authorial process, such as drafts, notes, version histories, and transcripts of A.I. assistance
units.why: "Students should save evidence of their authorial process, such as drafts, notes, version histories, and transcripts of A.I. assistance" requires keeping logs, P26.

units.passage: Ask students to include reflections on their methods at each stage, and to explain how the revisions at each stage respond to the peer or instructor feedback received at the previous stage.

units.passage: She allows students to use AI in her writing-heavy courses, but requires them to disclose and reflect on their AI use through what she calls an "AI consultation form."
units.policy: Students must disclose and reflect on their AI use through an "AI consultation form."
units.why: "requires them to disclose and reflect on their AI use through what she calls an AI consultation form". The form gathers reflections, so P26.

units.passage: Document usage of AI tools for transparency and accountability.
units.policy: Document usage of AI tools for transparency and accountability.

units.passage: Maintain detailed records of GenAI use, especially when personal data is involved

units.passage: Encourage students to save records of their progress over time (e.g., intermediate products, logs of work process), especially if generative AI is fully prohibited in your course
units.why: 'Encourage students to save records of their progress over time' asks for process records, P26 though they are kept as evidence, not submitted.
units.fit_note: Records of the work process to protect students if AI is banned, not records of AI use. Records are kept by students as protection when AI is prohibited, not submitted with work.

units.passage: Assignments that ask students to reflect on their use of AI tools (how and why they used them, what worked, what didn’t
units.why: 'Assignments that ask students to reflect on their use of AI tools (how and why they used them, what worked, what didn't)' recommends reflections on AI use (P26); instructor, before-course, informs.

units.why: 'whether to require students to turn in, or at least retain, AI chat transcripts' is a transcript option for instructors (P26).
